> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/search-filter.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ce2e369988c43cd36710de33b86527033646891` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1663475f099c53afc00831f00a1e11e2df0828f7` — the merge of head `07f0f4975f9b8ed04b87db4865483455c9558bef` into base `2ce2e369988c43cd36710de33b86527033646891`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1663475f099c53afc00831f00a1e11e2df0828f7 && git checkout 1663475f099c53afc00831f00a1e11e2df0828f7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2ce2e369988c43cd36710de33b86527033646891 07f0f4975f9b8ed04b87db4865483455c9558bef && git checkout -B drift-repro 2ce2e369988c43cd36710de33b86527033646891 && git merge --no-ff 07f0f4975f9b8ed04b87db4865483455c9558bef

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ce2e369988c43cd36710de33b86527033646891
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2ce2e369988c43cd36710de33b86527033646891` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `07f0f4975f9b8ed04b87db4865483455c9558bef`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/search-filter.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-search-empty-set.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts + packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts, packages/objectql/src/secret-fields.ts, packages/core/src/utils/internal-write-response.ts, packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts, packages/rest/src/error-response.ts, packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts, packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/import-template.ts, packages/client/src/query-builder.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/engine-findone-predicate.ts, packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx, .changeset/config.json, .objectui-sha, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, .github/workflows/pr-automation.yml, .github/workflows/lint.yml, and in objectui at 5e15928b (the pin the consumer pointer cites): packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx, packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx, packages/fields/src/widgets/useRecordQuery.ts, packages/data-objectstack/src/index.ts. The two `.changeset/24284-*.md` files are the prose face, judged under ②.

Inputs: card #24284 (body; comments 6248115403 triage, 6248247765 claim, 6248278272 dispatch, 6249664223 `os-dev-report` read as claims, 6249716675 re-declared claim), the filing finding ③.7 of record 6247399985 on PR #24274, PR #24320 (body, 6-file list), the net diff `git diff 2ce2e36998 pr/24320` (merge base 2ce2e36998 is origin/main at the fetch; +340/−5, byte-matching the report's per-file line budget), and the head's check-runs. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

Check-runs at read time (2026-10-18T12:08Z): 23 runs. 10 completed success: Check Changeset (the `changeset-check` job that runs `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base MERGE_BASE` and `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base MERGE_BASE`), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Auto Label, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, and the four claim/card guards. 1 skipped by design (Packed-tarball smoke). 12 in progress and not waited on: every Lint job (PM dispatch-gates, ESLint, docs & code guards — the job hosting `check:error-status-conformance` and `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` —, repo & tooling gates, CI/release & engine gates, the three scoped jobs) and the four Type Check jobs. No Build or Test Core run is in the listing at read time. Those runs are the gate verdict on the new pins and the moved code; this record does not stand in for them.

### ① Derived judgments

1. One judgement, one site — RIGHT. `ObjectQL.expandSearchOnAst` (engine.ts) now throws `emptySearchSetError(ast.object, schema, internalExcluded)` — the third argument is "the object declares at least one `internal: true` field" — in the branch where `expandSearchToFilter` answered `null` AND `normalizeSearch(raw).query.trim()` is non-empty. `expandSearchToFilter` returns `null` for exactly two reasons (blank query at its first line; `searchFields.length === 0` after `resolveSearchFields`), so with the blank case excluded the remaining reason is the empty resolved set, judged on the set the expansion itself resolved. `expandSearchToFilter` itself is unchanged in code (docblock only) and stays pure. Every verb reaches the site: `find` (engine.ts line 13965) and `findOne` (line 14286) call it directly; `count` (line 19881) and `aggregate` (line 20024) call it through `expandSearchOnOptions`, the carrier that holds only `object`, `where`, `search`, `searchFields`.

2. Exactly what flips from 200 to 400: a non-blank `search` (a string, or an object form with a non-blank `query`/`q`) on an object whose resolved search set is empty — no `searchableFields` entry naming an existing, non-virtual, non-internal field, and no non-hidden, non-internal field of a `SEARCHABLE_TEXTUAL_TYPES`/`SEARCHABLE_ENUM_TYPES` type outside `SEARCH_AUTO_EXCLUDED_FIELDS`. Doors, each traced to the engine: REST list GET and query POST (`findData` passes `search: options.search` to `engine.find` at protocol.ts 14718 and to `engine.count` for the paged `total` at 14862; `find` throws first, so the count's try/catch fallback is never reached); the grouped read (`aggregate`); the dispatcher and the SDK (`QueryBuilder.search` writes `query.search = { query, ...options }`, a passthrough to the data door); a hook body's `ctx.api.object(...).find/findOne` (body-runner.ts 1010–1017 call `ql.find` directly). `findOne` flips from a worse answer than 200-every-row: `searchIsPredicate` (engine-findone-predicate.ts) counts a non-blank term as a predicate, so a junction-object `findOne({ search })` used to pass the predicate guard and return the FIRST row of the whole object under `limit: 1` (the #4419 shape); it is now refused before the guard. The export route (`GET /data/:object/export?search=`) hands the term to `findData` inside its chunk loop (data-action-routes.ts 1127–1143), so the refusal is reached — see ③.4 for what the wire then carries.

3. What stays as it was — RIGHT, and pinned. A blank or whitespace term (`''`, `'   '`, `{ query: '  ' }`) is not a search: `raw != null` enters the block, `expandSearchToFilter` returns `null` on the blank check, and the throw is guarded by the same trim, so `where` is untouched (pin: 5 rows, count 5, `where` composes). An empty explicit override (`searchFields=''` or `[]`): the door's `assertSearchFieldsAreSearchable` returns on `names.length === 0` (unchanged), and `resolveSearchFields` treats an empty requested list as absent — on an object WITH a set the search runs over that set as before; on an object WITHOUT one it reaches the refusal (the PR's `?search=Dune&searchFields=` row, measured 400). The #4254 and #22646 refusals of a NAMED field fire at the data door before the engine and are untouched in the diff (`assertSearchFieldsAreSearchable` 13539–13660 at the head is byte-identical to the base). A `searchFields` naming the formula title still answers the gate's own `virtual` INVALID_FIELD. An object with a searchable field filters exactly as before (control pin: `Dune` → `b1`, `zzzz-nothing` → 0).

4. Decided from the declaration alone — RIGHT. `emptySearchSetError` reads `ast.object`, the registry schema's `searchableFields` array, the two type vocabularies and a boolean "this object declares an `internal: true` field"; no caller context, no permission answer, no row (pin: the driver is never read on any verb). The refusal is therefore the same for every caller through every door. What the message names is metadata the object declares, never a value — the posture of the sibling declaration gates (`assertOrderByIsMaterializable`, the dotted-projection refusal, #4254 at the door), all of which also run before the security middlewares. The `internal: true` parenthetical reveals only that some internal column exists; the describe door does not withhold the field's existence (protocol.ts has no describe-side internal strip; #22646 withholds the VALUE), so nothing new is disclosed.

5. An explicit `searchFields` whose names are all intersected away — RIGHT, two answers by door, both unchanged in direction. Through the data door, a name outside the allowed set is refused by #4254 before the engine (unchanged). To a direct engine caller, `resolveSearchFields` keeps its tolerant posture: when the intersection is empty but `allowed` is non-empty it falls back to the allowed set, a FILTERED answer, never every row (control pin: `searchFields: ['nope']` on `lib_book` answers `b2` for `emma`). It reaches the new refusal only when `allowed` is itself empty (pin: `['title']`, `['book']`, `['nope']`, `[]` on the junction all refused). So no override can rescue an object with no set, and no override on an object with a set changes answer.

6. `searchAll`'s skip input is the engine's scan set — RIGHT, and the palette keeps `200`. The engine builds `scanFields` as `schema.fields` minus `collectInternalReadFields(schema)` (objectql `secret-fields.ts`: `def.internal === true`) and resolves over that. The skip at protocol.ts 15862–15874 now builds `fieldMetaByName` minus `collectInternalWriteResponseFields(obj)` (core `internal-write-response.ts`: `def.internal === true`, documented as the cross-package twin "restated rather than imported" because objectql depends on metadata-protocol), then calls the same `resolveSearchFieldResolution` with the same `searchableFields` and the same `nameField ?? displayNameField` precedence, and `continue`s on an empty set before any query. Same metadata (`type`, `hidden`, `options`, `internal` ride on each `fields` entry), same filters, same answer; the FLS narrowing (`getQueryableFields`) that follows only ever hands the engine a subset of that set, so the engine's intersection cannot be empty when the skip was passed. Pinned over a real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` on a real `ObjectQL`: {book, loan, internal-only} → the book's hit, `totalObjects: 1`, no read of the other two; {loan, internal-only} → `200`, `totalObjects: 0`. The PR body's "same flag reader the #22646 ingress gate uses" is true (`assertSearchFieldsAreSearchable` at 13592 uses the core twin); the engine's own reader is the objectql twin, and the equivalence rests on the two keeping one verdict, which both docblocks promise.

7. Internal producers that hand `search` to an object they did not choose — one, and it skips. A `git grep` over every published package's `src` (tests excluded) finds `search:` as a query key at three protocol.ts sites (`findData`'s find and count, `searchAll`'s `search: q`) and nowhere else; http-dispatcher.ts 2392 `search: searchRegistered` is a capability flag, not a term; MCP, runtime, flows (service-automation `crud-nodes.ts` names `search` only as an icon) and analytics emit no `search` key; import by-name resolution does not use it. The export route hands the CALLER's own term to the caller's own object. No internal caller fails on this change.

8. Public surface — nothing widens. `emptySearchSetError` is module-private; the three new imports in engine.ts (`normalizeSearch`, the two type sets) already existed on `search-filter.ts`; protocol.ts adds no export; the error's own shape (`status`, `httpStatus`, `code`, `object`, `param`) is the shape the door's #4254/#22646 refusals already carry. The accept set of the data read narrows; no spec key, export or authorable spelling moves.

9. The wire — RIGHT at both doors. `resolveThrownHttpError` (types `thrown-http-error.ts` 206) reads `.status` (400) and keeps `.code` when it parses as `ErrorCode`; `INVALID_FIELD` is a `StandardErrorCode` member (spec `errors.zod.ts` 56), so `error.code` is `INVALID_FIELD` with no `declaredCode` demotion. The REST door reads it through `error-response.ts` and the dispatcher through `HttpDispatcher.errorFromThrown` (1240), one resolver for both — which is why the dev's "both transports" measured over REST GET/POST, with the dispatcher/SDK/hook doors covered by engine-level pins, is a sound reading (③.2). The catalog documents `INVALID_FIELD` as 400 (error-catalog.mdx 144, quick-reference row 966), so `check:error-status-conformance` has nothing new to reconcile.

10. The code: `INVALID_FIELD`, not `INVALID_QUERY` — RIGHT. `invalidQueryError`'s own docblock (protocol.ts 4874–4883) reserves `INVALID_QUERY` for aggregation-axis SHAPE mistakes "not about any FIELD", and the catalog's entry (320) says the same; `INVALID_FIELD`'s entry already carries every `searchFields` refusal on this axis. The request here is well-formed; the fact that cannot be honoured is the object's field declaration. One code per axis, no new catalog entry, no spec edit — as the dispatch required.

### ② Semver level

Two changesets, read against the diff, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` and `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`. Both packages are in the one `fixed` group (`.changeset/config.json`, 73 members). The `Check Changeset` check-run is success on this head, and that job runs both the level axis and the ADR-0087 registration gate; its conclusion is CI's verdict.

- `@objectstack/objectql` `minor` — RIGHT. The data read's accept set narrows, which is BREAKING; under the launch-window rule a breaking change ships `minor` with the breaking-ness carried by the `feat(objectql)!:` summary (the gate's `bang` signal) and by the ADR-0087 disposition, never by `major`. The disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is the honest category: no spec key, export, stored shape or authorable spelling is added, removed or renamed, and the body carries no arrow rewrite, FROM/TO pair or rewrite table for `findMigrationPrescription` to contradict it; the "What to do" paragraph is a metadata remedy, not a code rewrite. The body's claims match the diff: the two reasons a set is empty, every verb and door named in ①.2, the four unchanged cases of ①.3, and "Global search still passes over an object with nothing to scan". One wording note, not a defect: "the default set (the name/title field and the text, … and select fields)" reads as if the name/title field is always in the set; `autoDefaultFields` only LEADS with it when it is itself of a scannable type (#4483). The runtime message is exact.
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `patch` — RIGHT. The palette's accept set is unchanged (`200` before and after); what changes is the answer for an object whose only text column is internal — from that object's first `perObject` rows served as hits (the pre-existing cliff the skip's own docblock names) to being passed over — a bug fix, non-breaking, no `!`, no marker owed, and "What to do. Nothing." is true.
- The declaration. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and in the objectql changeset — RIGHT on both limbs: nothing widens (①.8), the accept set narrows. By `judgeLevel` a `no (narrowing)` carries the axis, objectql graded `minor` discharges it and metadata-protocol's `patch` is set aside as the residual — verdict `discharged`, exit 0, which is what the green check-run says. This is also what made the review owed at this tier (the committed tree touches no published schema and no governed path — Governed Surface Queue Guard success).
- PR title `fix(objectql)!:` against changeset summary `feat(objectql)!:` — both carry the bang; the type word differs. Cosmetic; no gate reads it.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. H2, `INVALID_FIELD` vs `INVALID_QUERY` (open question 1, shipped A) — ANSWERED, right; ①.10.

2. The `searchAll` skip input (open question 2, shipped A; the one deviation from the claim's "docblock only") — ANSWERED, right and necessary. Without it the refusal would have failed the whole sweep for an internal-only object, a worse regression than the one fixed; the one-line alignment keeps a single answer to "what the engine scans" and keeps the palette `200`. The seat re-declared the surface for exactly this line (claim 6249716675), so it is inside the claim at this head. The report's `out_of_scope_findings` entry — the pre-change palette served an internal-only object's first rows as hits — is REAL at the merge base (the skip judged over fields including internal ones; the engine then excluded them, expanded to nothing, and `find` returned unfiltered rows) and is correctly fixed in place rather than filed.

3. The console pointer (open question 3; `consumer_pointer`) — TRUE in substance at the pin it cites, with one stale fact. Read at objectui 5e15928b: `ListView.tsx` 1607 `showSearch: ua?.search !== false && !searchlessViewOnScreen` (the box is shown unless `userActions.search === false`; nothing consults the resolved set — true); `useRecordQuery.ts` 200 sets `params.$search`; `data-objectstack/src/index.ts` 4925–4926 maps `$search` to the `search` query parameter of `GET /api/v1/data/OBJECT` (so the wire spelling the pointer gives is right); `ObjectGrid.tsx` 2944 sends `$search` and, at 5888–5890, derives `searchEnabled` from `schema.searchableFields` when declared, else `showSearch ?? true` — so a junction object with no declaration still offers search there too; the pointer's "never consults the resolved search set" is attributed to ListView and is true of it. The stale fact: the pointer says "pinned `.objectui-sha` 5e15928b", but the head under review pins `0707b4ae37120d45d6401170666a0b76cb7a3546` (main moved the pin in #24311, `f5e98a35d1`, after the dev's last merge; the dev's `fd4e073a6c` still pinned 5e15928b). Not blocking — no objectui edit is in this PR and the pointer's prescription (hide quick-search and picker type-ahead when `resolveSearchFieldResolution` over the schema, internal fields excluded, is empty; else render the refusal) does not depend on the pin — but the adopting seat routes it naming the current pin and re-reads the four files there.

4. The export door, a correction to the PR body's H3 table — not blocking. (a) The `import-template` row is WRONG: in template mode (`?template=true` on the export path) `search` is in `TEMPLATE_INAPPLICABLE_PARAMS` (import-template.ts 292–294) and `readTemplateMode` answers `refused` → `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` before any row is read (data-action-routes.ts 872–875). That door never reaches the engine and is unchanged by this PR; it does not "surface the refusal". (b) The `export` row is right for `format=csv` and only loosely right for `json`/`xlsx`: the route sets its headers, writes `[` for json (1109) and opens the xlsx stream (1110) BEFORE the first `findData` of the loop (1143), and its catch (1255–1259) says in its own words that once headers are sent "the client receives a truncated stream which signals failure". So a junction-object `?search=` export flips from "200, every row" to: a `400 INVALID_FIELD` envelope via `handleRouteError` on csv (headers set, not flushed), and a committed 200 followed by a truncated stream on json (xlsx depends on whether the stream writes on open; not traced). This is the route's pre-existing posture for EVERY refusal `findData` throws inside the loop (#4254's own `searchFields` refusal, a filter refusal, a 403) and is loud rather than silent, so it meets the card's Expected; but it is not the 400-with-remedy the body claims for that door. ESCALATED as a one-line card candidate for the owning lane (dedupe words: export first chunk before headers; export refusal truncated stream): defer the first write until the first `findData` returns. The dev's own "NOT MEASURED over HTTP" flag on export was honest.

5. Message precision — not blocking, two notes for a later pass. (a) The auto branch says "none of its fields is a type the default search scans" when the set is empty; an object whose only text column is `hidden: true`, or carries a name in `SEARCH_AUTO_EXCLUDED_FIELDS` (`space`, `company_id`, …), is refused with that sentence although the TYPE is scannable — the field is excluded by flag or by name. (b) The `('internal: true' fields are never searched)` parenthetical is keyed on "the object declares any internal field", not on "an internal field of a scannable type was left out", so it appears for an internal lookup too. Both are wording, decided from the declaration, and prescribe the right remedy.

6. Error catalog — docs pointer, not blocking. `INVALID_FIELD`'s **Cause** text (error-catalog.mdx 144–161) lists the `searchFields` refusals but not "a search over an object with no searchable field".
